the question of how youngsters define the phenomenon of cyberbullying.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“cyberbully is an online or offline action, performed in the context of an unequal relationship, with the purpose of hurting another, and which is perceived as hurtful by the recipient.”
“cyberbully” is a person who repeatedly uses ICT to hurt someone, in a relationship where there is a power imbalance.

“cyberbully” is a term used to describe the perpetrator of an online or offline negative act that is perceived as hurtful, is intended to hurt, is repetitive, and is carried out by an individual or group of individuals who hold a power position over the victim, based on either offline power criteria or ICT-related power criteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyberbullying is a phenomenon that is characterized by the use of ICTs, but not limited to it.
cyberbullying is a form of bullying that takes place in the digital world.
cyberbullying is not a specific type of bullying, but a general term that refers to a wide range of negative online actions that can take different forms and have different characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of cyberbullying is not well defined and that youngsters’ perceptions are often inconsistent with the definitions used by researchers and policy makers.
youngsters are aware of the complexity of the phenomenon and are able to identify the key elements of cyberbullying, even if they do not use the term “cyberbul-lying” themselves.
the definition of cyberbullying should be based on the perception of the young people who experience it.
